title: Level 3 (Advanced) - B-23
notes:
West leads the ♣J against 4♠. South has 2 certain heart losers and 1 certain diamond loser. In order to make the contract, South must play the trump suit for no losers. The ♠Q must be found.

The normal way to play this spade holding is to cash the ♠K and then finesse against the hoped for ♠Q in East's hand. On this deal, it is correct to cash the ♠A and ♠K, playing West for doubleton ♠Q.

South has several inferences that combine to imply that West has the ♠Q. Nothing can be done if the ♠Q is twice guarded. East is marked with the ♣Q after West's lead of the ♣J.

West must hold the ♥A. If East has the ♥A, that card plus the ♣Q would be enough to respond to his partner's opening bid. As West would have led a heart if he was dealt both the ♥A and ♥K, East must have the ♥K.

As East has the ♥K and ♣Q, West must have the ♠Q. If East also had the ♠Q, he would have 7 high card points. He would not have passed West's 1 heart bid. As West must have the ♠Q, South should plan to cash the ♠K and ♠A, hoping West has only 2 spades.
